column1: # Tool pins for the Kalamari curation-triage tool.
# One row per pinned conda ENVIRONMENT, not per tool key.  The environment is the
# thing that is actually pinned: a lockfile recreates a whole prefix, and the two
# Yersinia/Listeria MLST tool keys in typers.py (mlst_yersinia, mlst_listeria) run
# the same binary out of the same prefix, so giving them two rows would claim two
# pins where there is one artifact.  That is why 11 rows cover 12 tool keys: the 9
# typer environments plus skani and the NCBI datasets CLI.
# marker_manifest.tsv answers "what does a marker call depend on"; this file answers
# "what exactly is installed, and how do I get it back".  They overlap on the nine
# typers and a test asserts they agree, so a bumped build cannot be recorded in one
# file and forgotten in the other.
# Every value below was READ FROM THE INSTALLED ENVIRONMENT on 2026-08-04 -- the
# builds come from the lockfiles, the versions from running each binary, and the
# AMRFinderPlus database version from `amrfinder --database_version` run INSIDE the
# pinned prefix.  Nothing here is copied from documentation.
# Columns
#   tool               environment / tool name, as typers.py and setup_envs.sh spell it
#   env                conda environment directory name under --env-dir
#   conda_package      package that gives the environment its purpose
#   conda_build        that package's exact version-build, as recorded in the lockfile
#   binary             executable under <env-dir>/<env>/bin
#   version_command    how to ask the tool its version; `none` = the tool cannot say
#   expected_version   version the tool must report; always the lockfile's build version
#   lockfile           repo-relative path to the explicit lockfile
#   lockfile_sha256    sha256 of that lockfile -- the immutable digest for the update gate
#   database_kind      bundled | post-install | runtime-download | none
#   database_version   the database identity that must be recorded with a call
#   database_digest    the evidence behind that identity -- see below
#   notes              why this pin looks the way it does
# database_kind is the operational question "is this environment self-sufficient?"
#   bundled          the database ships inside the conda package, so the lockfile pins it
#   post-install     the database is fetched after install and pinned by its own version
#   runtime-download the tool fetches data at run time; the lockfile does NOT pin it
#   none             the tool has no reference database
# database_digest answers the next question: what PROVES that identity?  A version
# string is only a label -- anybody can make a directory and name it 2026-05-15.1 --
# so every row carries the strongest evidence its situation allows:
#   in-lockfile      bundled: the database travels inside the conda package, so
#                    lockfile_sha256 is already its digest
#   sha256:<64 hex>  post-install: one roll-up digest over every file of the dated
#                    database, each file listed with its own sha256 in
#                    src/curation-triage/amrfinderplus_db_manifest.tsv
#   unpinned         runtime-download: the data is fetched when the tool runs, and
#                    nothing pins it (ECTyper's Zenodo sketch)
#   n/a              the tool has no database
# setup_envs.sh checks the amrfinderplus database file by file against that manifest,
# not just against the version string, and names the files that differ.
# Two honest gaps this table records rather than hides:
#   1. AMRFinderPlus keeps its dated database outside the conda package, so no conda
#      lockfile can capture it, and `amrfinder -u` only ever fetches the LATEST one.
#      2026-05-15.1 is therefore FROZEN rather than re-downloadable: setup_envs.sh
#      provisions it into the pinned prefix and verifies all 162 files against the
#      committed manifest.  That proves SAMENESS, not availability -- if the local
#      copy is lost and NCBI has moved on, this exact database cannot be fetched
#      again, and the manifest can then only say that whatever turns up is not it.
#   2. ECTyper downloads a 943 MiB MASH sketch from Zenodo on first use.  It is
#      deliberately NOT provisioned: ECTyper is context-only, decisive planning never
#      selects it, so the pinned pipeline never reaches the code path that needs it.
# Update gate: changing any conda_build, expected_version, lockfile_sha256 or
# database_version is a pin change.  It enters production only after (1) the artifact
# has an immutable digest, (2) the fixed validation panel is re-run, (3) every call
# difference is classified as software / database / threshold / rule, and (4) this
# file and the changelog are updated.
# database_digest is EVIDENCE, and today it is not yet part of a component identity.
# update_gate.py builds db:<env> from database_version alone, and the two other places
# that record the AMRFinderPlus database -- marker_manifest.tsv and the Tier-2 caches'
# own amrfinder_database_version -- carry the plain dated string, so putting the digest
# into database_version would fail points 1 and 2 rather than tighten them.  A database
# swapped underneath an unchanged version string is therefore caught by setup_envs.sh,
# not by the gate.  Folding the digest into the identity is a small, separate change:
# make pin_state build db:<env> as `<database_version>+db:<first 12 hex of
# database_digest>`, keep the marker-manifest and cache comparisons on the version part
# only, and add the db:amrfinderplus changelog row that accepts the new identity.
tool
shigeifinder
column13: `shigeifinder --version` exits 2 and prints a usage message, so the tool can never confirm its own version and the recorded version stays shigeifinder@unknown; 1.3.4 here is the conda build, which is the only checkable identity. The installed dist-info disagrees and says 1.3.2. The environment also needs setuptools, which the lockfile carries, or the tool dies on `import pkg_resources`.

column1: btyper3
column13: The bundled PubMLST copy is dated inside the package and cannot be refreshed without changing the build, which is exactly what makes the lockfile a database pin as well as a software pin.

column1: lissero
column13: Prints `LisSero 0.4.10`. It shells out to makeblastdb from the same prefix, so the prefix bin must be first on PATH, not just the binary called by absolute path.

column1: sistr
column13: Prints `sistr_cmd 1.1.3`; no flag reports the database version, so it is read from the bundled dbstatus.txt. setuptools is pinned at 80.10.2 because sistr imports pkg_resources, which setuptools 81 deprecates and a later release drops.

column1: seqsero2
column13: The executable keeps its .py suffix, so the binary name is not the tool name.

column1: ectyper
column13: Prints `ectyper 2.0.0 running database version 1.0`, so the FIRST version token is the software and the last is the database. The O/H alleles and pathotype table are bundled, but the MASH species sketch is a 943 MiB Zenodo download at run time, which is why the kind is runtime-download. It is deliberately not provisioned: ECTyper is context-only and is never planned as a decisive task.

column1: amrfinderplus
column13: The only tool here with a first-class dated database, so a changed call is attributable to a database update rather than to biology. The database lives outside the conda package and no lockfile can capture it; setup_envs.sh provisions it into <env-dir>/amrfinderplus/share/amrfinderplus/data/latest and then checks `amrfinder --database_version`. `amrfinder -u` fetches the LATEST database, which may not be this one, so 2026-05-15.1 is FROZEN: the digest column is the roll-up over all 162 files (239.4 MB), each one listed in src/curation-triage/amrfinderplus_db_manifest.tsv, and setup_envs.sh compares the installed database against it file by file and names any that differ. The digest proves the database is the same one; it cannot make NCBI serve this version again.

column1: abricate
column11: vfdb 4592 seqs, plasmidfinder 488 seqs, both dated 2026-Apr-3
column13: A Perl script: without the prefix bin first on PATH it dies with `Can't locate Path/Tiny.pm`, which looks like a broken install and is really a missing PATH entry.

column1: mlst
column13: One prefix serves both typers.py tool keys, mlst_listeria and mlst_yersinia; they differ only by --scheme. Also a Perl script, so the same PATH rule as abricate applies.

column1: skani
column13: Supplies ANI and aligned fraction for every Tier-2 panel comparison. marker_manifest.tsv does not list it because it answers no marker question, but its version moves calls, so it is pinned here.

column1: datasets
column13: Prints `datasets version: 18.34.0`. It comes from conda-forge, not bioconda, unlike every other pin here. It has no database; it queries the NCBI API, so it needs network at cache-build time and nothing at replay time.
